subject: design-technology
title: Applications: Metal and Polymer Processes
welcome_lead: Move from forge to injection moulder and discover how metals and polymers are shaped at scale.
meta_desc: Apply metal and polymer manufacturing processes to real GCSE D&T contexts.
final_note: You can pick the right metal or polymer process for batch or mass production.

concepts.def: Shaping hot metal by hammering or pressing.
Pouring molten metal into a mould.
Joining metals with a low-melt filler.
Forcing molten polymer into a mould.
Sucking heated polymer sheet onto a mould.
Inflating a polymer tube inside a mould.

walkthroughs.body_html: Forging aligns metal grains, giving tough crankshafts. Casting handles complex shapes like engine blocks. Soldering joins copper plumbing and electronics, while welding and brazing handle stronger structural joints.

Injection moulding makes high-volume parts like Lego bricks. Blow moulding creates hollow products like fizzy-drink bottles. Vacuum forming drapes a softened sheet over a mould — used for chocolate trays and bath tubs.

walkthroughs.h2: Which process for a yoghurt pot?
walkthroughs.body_html: A yoghurt pot is thin-walled, open-topped, made in millions. Injection moulding or vacuum forming work — vacuum forming wins on cost per unit for thin pots, injection moulding for high-detail lids.
